title: Marburg Virus Disease in Rwanda, 2024 — Public Health ...
snippet: previous filovirus disease outbreaks suggest that familiarity with infected patients, high emotional burden, and emergency clinical interventions may contribute to lapses in infection prevention and control measures.21 Improvements in the capacity for testing and earlier consideration of MVD in the differential diagnosis of severe febrile illness are also necessary, particularly in high-risk regions where viral hemorrhagic fever may initially be unrecognized and mimic other endemic febrile [...] The prevention of high mortality in future filovirus disease outbreaks will require faster recognition of viral hemorrhagic fevers through a One Health approach involving collaboration among community health workers, human health and genomics specialists, bat biologists, ecologists, conservationists, and other relevant experts. Such an effort will strengthen infection prevention and control measures, reduce the risk of nosocomial transmission, and ensure timely delivery of supportive and [...] The deployment of the ChAd3-MARV vaccine within 13 days after declaration of the outbreak, alongside a concurrent phase 2 clinical trial, shows that investigational vaccines can be integrated into an outbreak response. Although the effect of the vaccine on transmission was not assessed directly, the prioritization of frontline workers for emergency vaccination under an adapted WHO Solidarity core protocol provides an important model for responses to future filovirus disease outbreaks.
